headline: One Day of Eating in Colonia Juárez, Booked and Walked in Order
article_markdown:
Colonia Juárez is not a secret. Handshake Speakeasy, on Amberes, was voted the world's best bar in 2024 and has been in the top two of North America's list since. Churrería El Moro, in business since 1935, has had a branch at Génova 59 for years. What Juárez has that Roma Norte doesn't is compression: the six places below sit inside a few blocks of each other, on streets named for European cities, and you can do the whole thing on foot without once opening a map for a fifteen-minute walk between courses.

The concrete case, since it should be earned rather than asserted: Elena Reygadas runs two Panadería Rosetta bakeries in Roma, and both are queue-on-the-pavement operations. Her Juárez room, Café Nin at Havre 73, sells the same bread and gives you a table and a fourteen-hour day to use it. El Moro has outposts in both neighbourhoods. Juárez isn't holding back anything Roma has. It just puts it closer together and makes you stand in line less.

**Pick a Wednesday, Thursday, Friday or Saturday.** Havre 77 is closed Mondays and stops serving at 6pm on Sundays, and the backup bar at the end only opens Wednesday to Saturday. Every other day breaks the route.

### 9am, Café Nin, Havre 73

A high-ceilinged room built to be sat in for hours, modelled on twentieth-century literary cafés, with Rosetta's bread coming out all day. Open 7am to 9pm Monday to Wednesday, to 10pm Thursday to Saturday, per Reygadas's own site.

Language: easiest stop of the day. The pastries are in a case. Point. The guava-and-cheese rol and the pan de pulque are the ones to point at, and the chilaquiles if you want a plate rather than a paper bag.

### 12:30pm, El Pescadito, Estocolmo 29

Sonoran fried fish and shrimp tacos, ordered at a counter, eaten standing at a rail. This is the stop your Spanish nerves were invented for and it's the one that will cure them, because the transaction is roughly three words long. Say "pescado" or "camarón," pay, and take the taco to the bar of salsas, pickled onions, cabbage and crema, where you finish it yourself with no conversation at all.

Open 11am to 6pm Monday to Friday, 10am to 6pm at weekends. It closes at six every day, so this can't slide to dinner.

### 3:30pm, Cicatriz, Dinamarca 44

One of the first wine bars in the city, run by the Lindemans, a sister and brother from New York. Small, bright, scuffed in a lived-in way, with a menu that leans vegetable-heavy and a genuinely good coffee programme. Open 9am to midnight daily and it takes no reservations at all, which is exactly what you want in the middle of an afternoon.

Language: staff and half the room speak English. If you've had a morning of pointing, this is where you get to ask a question and be answered.

### 6:30pm, Havre 77, Havre 77

A restored nineteenth-century house turned French brasserie, with an oyster bar and the kind of dining room that makes the Porfirian bones of this neighbourhood legible. Onion soup, oysters, duck. Tue–Thu 2pm to 10pm, Fri–Sat 2pm to 11pm.

One caution: the restaurant's own website is Spanish only and lists a phone number as the way to book. Book through its OpenTable page instead, which handles the whole thing in English before you leave home. Do book. The room is small and this is the one stop on the route where turning up cold may not work.

### 9pm, Churrería El Moro, Génova 59

Churros and thick cacao chocolate, made in front of you, at a counter, from an operation that has been doing only this since 1935. Order the chocolate *español* if you want it thick enough to stand a churro in.

The hours are the one thing I couldn't pin down cleanly: El Moro's own site gives this branch as 9am–11pm daily on one page and 8am–10pm Sunday to Thursday on another. Arrive before 10pm and both listings agree you're fine.

### 10pm, Handshake Speakeasy, Amberes 65

Unmarked door, Art Deco room, cocktails that justify the ranking. Reservations go through OpenTable only, open roughly two weeks ahead, and disappear fast. Book the moment your dates are fixed. Standard slot is ninety minutes, there's a fifteen-minute grace period, and parties of five or more pay a 250-peso-per-person deposit.

If you don't get a table, don't spend the evening hoping for a walk-in. Book Xaman, at Copenhague 6, a five-minute walk away, open 7pm to 2am Wednesday to Saturday and also bookable on OpenTable.

The whole route runs Havre to Estocolmo to Dinamarca, back to Havre, then down to Génova and Amberes. Nothing on it exceeds a ten-minute walk from the thing before it. Two of the six need advance booking, both done online in English, and both are worth doing weeks out. The other four you simply walk into.

- El Moro branch list, Génova 59 Col. Juárez, hours: [elmoro.mx/churrerias](https://elmoro.mx/churrerias/) (9am–11pm daily) and [elmoro.mx sucursales](https://elmoro.mx/category/sucursales/page/2/) (Sun–Thu 8am–10pm, Fri–Sat 8am–11pm). **The operator's own site contradicts itself on this branch's hours**, which is why the article gives a "before 10pm" instruction rather than a single closing time.
- Havre 77 hours and Spanish-only site with phone booking: [havre77.mx](https://havre77.mx/). Online booking available: [OpenTable](https://www.opentable.com/r/havre-77-mexico). Room and oyster bar: [The Infatuation, 26 Aug 2025](https://www.theinfatuation.com/mexico-city/guides/best-restauants-juarez-mexico-city)
- El Pescadito, Estocolmo 29, hours: [restaurantesencdmx.com](https://restaurantesencdmx.com/restaurante/el-pescadito-estocolmo-29-juarez) (Mon–Fri 11–18, Sat–Sun 10–18), corroborated by a second aggregator listing. Branch confirmed on [elpescadito.mx](https://elpescadito.mx/ubicaciones/en-cdmx/)
- Cicatriz, Dinamarca 44, 9am–midnight daily, no reservations: [cicatrizcafe.com](https://www.cicatrizcafe.com/). Lindeman ownership and wine-bar history: [The Infatuation](https://www.theinfatuation.com/mexico-city/reviews/cicatriz)
- Handshake Speakeasy address and rankings: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handshake_Speakeasy) (world's best bar 2024). Reservation terms, OpenTable-only, 90 minutes, 15-minute grace, 250-peso deposit for 5+: [handshake.bar](https://handshake.bar/reservation-terms-and-conditions/)
- Xaman Bar, Copenhague 6, Wed–Sat 7pm–2am: [OpenTable](https://www.opentable.com/r/xaman-bar-ciudad-de-mexico) listing and aggregator hours

Details I could not establish, and therefore did not assert:

- **El Pescadito's exact daily hours from the operator.** Its own locations page carries no hours; the article's times come from two agreeing third-party listings. Worth a check on the day.
- **Handshake's precise walk-in policy and closing time by day.** Reports of "arrive before opening" walk-ins are secondhand and not on the bar's own terms page, so the article tells the reader to book or go to Xaman rather than to try their luck.
- **Havre 77's counter/oyster-bar seating as bookable.** The oyster bar is documented; whether you can reserve a seat at it is not, so the article does not promise one.
- **Whether Havre 77's staff work in English.** Not verifiable from a source; the article routes the reader around the language risk at the booking stage instead of claiming the room is English-speaking.
- **The 50 Best Bars 2025 and 2026 standings** could not be read directly: theworlds50best.com was under planned maintenance until 9 September 2026 when accessed. The article uses only the 2024 world ranking, which Wikipedia carries.
- The brief's implied premise that Masala y Maíz anchors Juárez no longer holds: it is now listed at Artículo 123 #116 in Centro, so it is not on the route.
